our_title: V5 recursive wrapper dereferences a NULL ubvec that the Kway wrapper tolerates
ran:
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$WORK/build/lib (or build64/lib) ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1; cd $WORK/repro; ./build.sh $WORK/build (or build64); ./CLI-02/cli02
32-bit and 64-bit pristine: 'metis_graph_part.c:290:5: runtime error: load of null pointer of type const double' then 'AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000000 ... #0 _SCOTCH_METIS_PartGraph2 metis_graph_part.c:290 #2 SCOTCH_METIS_V5_PartGraphRecursive metis_graph_part.c:590'. './cli02 k' (Kway): ret=1 objval=80. Patched: 'Recursive: ret=1 objval=80' (64-bit: objval=82). After the series, in both trees: make -C <tree>/src/check ... check_libmetis_v3 check_libmetis_v5 check_libmetis_dual_v3 check_libmetis_dual_v5 check_libmetis_dual_f_v3 check_libmetis_dual_f_v5 check_scotch_arch check_scotch_graph_map check_scotch_graph_part_ovl (gcc) and check_libparmetis_v3 (mpicc, EXECP4='mpirun --oversubscribe -np 4'): all rc=0, 0 build warnings (build.log / build64.log). The new test_libmetis.c / test_libparmetis.c compiled against the pristine $INFRA/asan libraries fail (pristine_tests/: rc=1, archCmpltwArchBuild2 'invalid parameters (2)' + double free at the bwgttab call; the Recursive NULL-ubvec call crashes).
severity_note: same as review: public API argument documented optional by METIS 5, NULL on the most common call form, hard crash
evidence: metis_graph_part.c:592 'SCOTCH_STRATRECURSIVE, ubvec)' and :595 'SCOTCH_STRATRECURSIVE, ubvec));' versus the Kway wrapper :559 'SCOTCH_STRATDEFAULT, (ubvec != NULL) ? ubvec : &kbalval)'; :290 'SCOTCH_stratGraphMapBuild (&stradat, flagval, *nparts, *kbalval);'
upstream_change: none in 7.0.16..7.0.17 (no commit touches src/libscotchmetis). History: a026661 (2023-08-17) 'Allow users to pass a NULL ubvec vector in ... SCOTCH_METIS_V5_PartGraphKway()' fixed the Kway wrapper only; the Recursive twin was forgotten
review_accuracy: accurate (mechanism, lines, reproducer). Its Fix line (copy the Kway fallback) works as written, but keeps two divergent copies of the same wrapper body, which is how the Kway-only fix of 2023 missed this one, and leaves the ubvec unit error (CLI-03) in place; the two must be fixed together.
first_pass_critique: status, method, location and evidence correct. Its preferred fix (shared helper, under CLI-03) silently treats ubvec[0] <= 1.0 as 'default 0.01', hiding unit errors that real METIS rejects (CheckParams); its second option was never compiled. It did not propose merging the two wrapper bodies, which is the structural cause.

extra_instances.quote: *revaptr = SCOTCHMETISNAMES (METIS_V5_PartGraphRecursive) (nvtxs, ncon, xadj, adjncy, vwgt, vsize, adjwgt, nparts, tpwgts, ubvec, options, objval, part);

fix_options.label: a: NULL fallback in the Recursive wrapper (the review's fix)
fix_options.summary: Declare kbalval = 0.01 in METIS_V5_PartGraphRecursive and pass (ubvec != NULL) ? ubvec : &kbalval, as the Kway wrapper does.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Two lines; fixes the crash only, keeps the ubvec unit bug (CLI-03) and the duplicated wrapper bodies.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: It is exactly what he did for Kway in a026661, which is why it is not enough: the same omission would recur at the next change.

fix_options.label: b: default inside _SCOTCH_METIS_PartGraph2 when kbalval is NULL
fix_options.tradeoffs: One line, protects every caller, but duplicates the 0.01 default (V3 wrappers already set it) and hides the V5 contract in a routine shared with V3.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He keeps defaults at the API boundary (kbalval = 0.01 in each V3 wrapper); a NULL-tolerant internal routine is not his idiom.

fix_options.label: c: one common V5 routine that converts and checks the parameters (patch 0003)
fix_options.summary: _SCOTCH_METIS_V5_PartGraph() is the single body of both V5 wrappers; ubvec NULL gives the default tolerance, otherwise ubvec[0] is validated (> 1.0) and converted (CLI-03); ncon handled (CLI-07).
fix_options.tested: cli02 (both strategies), check_libmetis_v5 (3 graphs) 32/64-bit, new test case: Recursive with NULL tpwgts and ubvec
fix_options.tradeoffs: Larger diff; behaviour change for callers passing ubvec (now honoured) and ubvec <= 1 (now METIS_ERROR_INPUT).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Precedent: bfe5287 'Place MeTiS mapping metrics computation routines in separate functions' and 0ecabba 'Refactor MeTiS compatibility library' (he factors shared wrapper logic); unconditional checks on API-controlled values with SCOTCH_errorPrint + METIS_ERROR_INPUT as in metis_graph_part_dual.c:116-118.

cleanup_done: The two wrapper bodies are replaced by calls to the common routine; the kbalval local of the Kway wrapper and the duplicated baseval expression are gone. No struct field or macro involved.
test_added: src/check/test_libmetis.c (v5 section): METIS_PartGraphRecursive with tpwgts = NULL and ubvec = NULL, result checked by checkPart(). Pristine: crash.
notes: The V5 Fortran wrappers are pure pass-throughs and need no change.

our_title: V5 ubvec ratio used unconverted as Scotch tolerance: 1.05 allows twice the average load
severity_note: same as review: silent quality loss for every V5 caller that sets ubvec (the usual call form); the maintainer's own test used 0.05, i.e. the Scotch convention, which shows the units were never reconciled
location_7_0_17: src/libscotchmetis/metis_graph_part.c:559,562 (Kway) and :592,595 (Recursive) pass ubvec as kbalval; :290 uses *kbalval as the strategy tolerance; src/libscotch/kgraph_map_rb.c:140-141 apply it as (1 -/+ kbalval) * comploadrat
evidence: metis_graph_part.c:559 'SCOTCH_STRATDEFAULT, (ubvec != NULL) ? ubvec : &kbalval)'; :290 'SCOTCH_stratGraphMapBuild (&stradat, flagval, *nparts, *kbalval);'; kgraph_map_rb.c:140 'datadat.comploadmin = (1.0 - paraptr->kbalval) * grafptr->comploadrat;' :141 'datadat.comploadmax = (1.0 + paraptr->kbalval) * grafptr->comploadrat;'; src/check/test_libmetis.c:168 'const double kbaltab[1] = { 0.05 };'
review_accuracy: accurate on mechanism and effect. Its Fix line 'kbalval = max(ubvec[0] - 1.0, 0)' silently maps an invalid ratio (<= 1.0, e.g. the 0.05 of the shipped test) to a zero tolerance, i.e. demands perfect balance instead of reporting the caller's unit error; METIS 5.1 rejects ubvec[i] <= 1.0 (CheckParams). The review also omits that ParMETIS_V3_PartKway ignores ubvec altogether (it is mentioned only under CLI-07).
first_pass_critique: status and measurements correct and reproduced exactly. Its preferred helper treats ubvec[0] <= 1.0 as 'default 0.01' (silent, not METIS behaviour) and leaves the ParMETIS twin untouched although it is the same conversion; it did not notice that src/check/test_libmetis.c passes 0.05 (so its fix would silently change what the shipped test exercises); the alternative 'subtract 1 when > 1' heuristic is correctly rejected but was not written as a real diff.

extra_instances.quote: const float * const         ubvec,                /* Not used */ ... SCOTCH_stratInit (&stradat);  (default tolerance 0.05 from library_dgraph_map.c:180)

extra_instances.location: src/check/test_libparmetis.c:242 (dead block, SCOTCH_METIS_VERSION == 5 is never built for ParMETIS)

fix_options.label: a: subtract 1.0 in both V5 wrappers, no validation
fix_options.summary: kbalval = (ubvec != NULL) ? (ubvec[0] - 1.0) : 0.01 in both wrappers (also fixes CLI-02).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Minimal; a ratio <= 1 yields a negative tolerance (comploadmax < comploadrat: every part over-full, FM refinement degenerates) instead of an error; still two copies of the wrapper body; ParMETIS untouched.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Too lenient for an API-controlled value; he adds unconditional checks for those (b10825d 'Add parameter check to SCOTCH_dgraphRedist()').

fix_options.label: b: heuristic in _SCOTCH_METIS_PartGraph2: (*kbalval > 1.0) ? *kbalval - 1.0 : *kbalval
fix_options.summary: Treat values above 1 as METIS ratios inside the shared routine.
fix_options.tradeoffs: One line, but ambiguous: a V5 ratio of exactly 1.0 (perfect balance) and a legal V3 tolerance > 1 are misread; mixes two conventions in one routine.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would not take a heuristic on a documented unit.

fix_options.label: c: validate and convert in the common V5 routine; ParMETIS honours ubvec[0] (patch 0003)
fix_options.summary: kbalval = ubvec[0] - 1.0 after checking ubvec[0] > 1.0 (else SCOTCH_errorPrint + METIS_ERROR_INPUT); NULL gives 0.01; ParMETIS_V3_PartKway builds its strategy with SCOTCH_stratDgraphMapBuild (SCOTCH_STRATDEFAULT, procglbnbr, *nparts, ubvec[0] - 1.0), default 0.05 as before.
fix_options.tested: cli03 (table above), pcli07 (ParMETIS, ubvec 1.03), check_libmetis_v5 / check_libparmetis_v3 on bump, bump_b1, bump_imbal_32, 32/64-bit; shipped test's kbaltab changed to 1.05 (0.05 is now rejected, as in METIS)
fix_options.tradeoffs: Behaviour change: partitions for ubvec callers become tight (the point); ubvec <= 1 now fails with a message; the ParMETIS doc paragraph changes.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Mirrors the ParMETIS strategy-building idiom of the sequential code (metis_graph_part.c:289-290) and the dgraph default (library_dgraph_map.c:180); error reporting as metis_graph_part_dual.c:116-118.

cleanup_done: 'Not used' comments on ncon and ubvec in parmetis_dgraph_part.c removed (4 places); kbalval default centralised; test value 0.05 replaced by 1.05.
test_added: src/check/test_libmetis.c: kbaltab = 1.05 (METIS convention) for all v5 calls, plus checkLoad() on the ncon = 2 call (tolerance-driven balance of the first constraint); src/check/test_libparmetis.c: ubvec = {1.05, 1.05} call.
docs_updated: doc/src/ptscotch/p_l.tex (ParMETIS_V3_PartKway: ubvec[0] is used, ratio semantics stated)
notes: Not done on purpose: honouring options[METIS_OPTION_UFACTOR] when ubvec is NULL (METIS uses 1 + ufactor/1000, default 1.03 kway / 1.001 recursive). It would be a new feature changing the documented 'only NUMBERING and OBJTYPE are supported' statement; the Scotch default stays 0.01. The dead v5 block of test_libparmetis.c (kbaltab 0.05, tpwgtab undeclared) is left as is, see extra.json PS2-G25-2.

our_title: V5 routines use options[NUMBERING] = -1 verbatim as base value: endless loop or heap overflow
severity_note: review says medium; raised because the outcome is an endless loop or out-of-bounds reads, and filling the option array with -1 is the documented METIS 5 idiom (its METIS_SetDefaultOptions does exactly that); it is hidden only for callers using Scotch's own zero-filling METIS_SetDefaultOptions
location_7_0_17: src/libscotchmetis/metis_graph_part.c:554 and :587; metis_graph_order.c:183; metis_graph_part_dual.c:108-109; metis_options.c:70 (zero fill, documented in doc/src/scotch/s_l.tex:8942-8944)
evidence: metis_graph_part.c:554 'baseval = ((options != NULL) && (options != xadj)) ? options[METIS_OPTION_NUMBERING] : 0;' (identical at :587 and metis_graph_order.c:183); metis_graph_part_dual.c:108-109 'if ((options != NULL) && (options != ne)) baseval = options[METIS_OPTION_NUMBERING];'; metis_options.c:70 'memSet (options, 0, METIS_NOPTIONS * sizeof (SCOTCH_Num));'
review_accuracy: accurate but incomplete: metis_graph_order.c:183 (METIS_V5_NodeND) has the identical expression and is not listed; the Fix line (negative means 0, reject others than 0/1) is right, except that METIS's GETOPTION treats exactly -1 as 'default', not every negative value.
first_pass_critique: correct status and evidence, and it did find NodeND. Its preferred option normalises inside a helper private to metis_graph_part.c and says 'same 3-line normalisation' for the other two files, i.e. three copies of the logic; its second option (fill with -1 in METIS_SetDefaultOptions) would change a documented behaviour ('Other values are set to 0', s_l.tex:8944) and break the shipped tests that set options[NUMBERING] after it, which it did not mention. It treats all negative values as default rather than -1 only.

extra_instances.quote:
if ((options != NULL) && (options != ne))       /* For the Fortran interface, null arrays are those equal to ne */
    baseval = options[METIS_OPTION_NUMBERING];

extra_instances.location: src/libscotchmetis/metis_graph_part_dual.c:218 (OBJTYPE read without default handling; harmless for -1 since it is simply not VOL)

fix_options.label: a: inline normalisation at the four sites
fix_options.summary: At each site: value -1 means 0; then reject anything but 0/1 with SCOTCH_errorPrint + METIS_ERROR_INPUT.
fix_options.tradeoffs: No new file; four copies of the same five lines, which is how the three divergent copies arose in 9fe677a.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Plausible for him (9fe677a inlined the expression three times), but the fourth copy makes a helper the better choice.

fix_options.label: b: make METIS_SetDefaultOptions fill with -1 like METIS, plus normalisation
fix_options.summary: options[i] = -1 for all i; readers substitute defaults.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Closest to METIS, but changes the documented output of METIS_SetDefaultOptions (s_l.tex 'Other values are set to 0'); readers must be fixed anyway, so it adds risk without removing work.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He does not change documented behaviour for a bug that is fixed on the reading side.

fix_options.label: c: _SCOTCH_METIS_optionGet() in metis_options.c, used by the four readers (patch 0004)
fix_options.summary: SCOTCH_Num _SCOTCH_METIS_optionGet (options, nulltab, optinum, defaval) returns defaval when options is NULL, equals the Fortran null array, or holds -1; each caller then rejects a numbering outside 0..1. New metis_options.h declares it; Makefile dependencies updated (CMake lists only sources).
fix_options.tested: cli06 (all modes), check_libmetis_v3/v5/dual_v3/dual_v5/dual_f_v3/dual_f_v5 32/64-bit; new test: option array filled with -1 for PartGraphKway and NodeND
fix_options.tradeoffs: One new header and exported internal symbol; the PartMeshDual hunk is in a function that group G26 (CLI-05) also edits, on different lines.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same shape as metis_graph_part.h / metis_graph_dual.h internal helpers (_SCOTCH_METIS_OutputCut, _SCOTCH_METIS_MeshToDual2) declared in per-module headers; option handling belongs in metis_options.c.

cleanup_done: none needed (the duplicated expression is replaced at every site; no symbol orphaned)
test_added: src/check/test_libmetis.c (v5): options[] filled with -1 (NUMBERING forced to the graph base when it is not 0), METIS_PartGraphKway + METIS_NodeND, checked by checkPart/checkOrder. Pristine: endless loop.
notes: NUMBERING = 2 with 0-based arrays (num2) is a caller error that METIS rejects; libscotch itself handles base-2 graphs (gbase 2 + gpart run clean), so the heap overflow seen on pristine is the caller/library mismatch, now rejected.

our_title: Target weight conversion overflows to INT_MIN for arbitrary weights, then double-frees
severity_note: review says medium; raised because in 7.0.17 the failure path double-frees the caller's array (PS2-G25-1), so arbitrary tpwgts (computed fractions are the common case) corrupt the heap instead of merely failing
evidence: metis_graph_part.c:224-225 'doubtmp = doubadj / doubtmp; doubadj = (doubadj * doubtmp) / (double) intGcd ((int) round (doubadj), (int) round (doubtmp));' :229 'intetab[i] = (SCOTCH_Num) round (doubtab[i] * doubadj);'; parmetis_dgraph_part.c:101-102 same with floats
review_accuracy: accurate on mechanism. Its Fix line 'round(w * 1e6), minimum 1' would turn a zero target into 1 and change the integer ratios of exact inputs (0.5/0.5 -> 500000/500000); 'cap doubadj' is right but the cap must be tested before the gcd: the intermediate doubtmp = doubadj / fraction reaches 1e12 before the lcm is formed, so a cap applied after the gcd still performs an out-of-range (int) conversion.
first_pass_critique: evidence right (INT_MIN values reproduced). Its tested diff clamps every weight to >= 1 (its own text says to drop that) and caps only after intGcd ((int) round (doubtmp)) with the possibly-overflowing cast, so the UB it set out to remove remains at the step that blows up; DOUBADJMAX = 1e4 is too coarse (targets below 1e-4 round to 0 and are then rejected by archCmpltw); it named the float twin but did not patch it; it did not notice the double free that its own repro printed.

extra_instances.location: src/libscotch/arch_cmpltw.c:184 (new defect PS2-G25-1, reached by this one)

fix_options.label: a: always round at a fixed resolution (drop the common-denominator search)
fix_options.summary: intetab[i] = round (doubtab[i] * 1e6) in both converters; intGcd no longer used there.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Simplest and always in range, but exact ratios change (0.25/0.75 gives 250000/750000 instead of 1/3) so archCmpltw weights and partitions differ from 7.0.17 for every weighted call; the ParMETIS 'skip equal values' optimisation becomes moot.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He wrote the gcd search to keep small exact integers; dropping it changes results for all existing users.

fix_options.label: b: bound the factor at 1e6, tested before the gcd (patch 0002)
fix_options.summary: doubtmp = doubadj / fraction; if doubtmp <= DOUBADJMAX reduce by the gcd; if the result exceeds DOUBADJMAX, set doubadj = DOUBADJMAX and stop (fixed resolution); casts become (SCOTCH_Num). Same in the float twin (FLOTADJMAX).
fix_options.tested: cli08 6 1 / 3 2 32/64-bit, check_libmetis_v5 and check_libparmetis_v3 with a new 9-weight array without small common denominator (pristine fails on both)
fix_options.tradeoffs: Exact small ratios preserved; arbitrary weights rounded at 1e-6 (sum of integer weights about 1e6, far below Gnum range; kgraph uses doubles for comploadavg).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Keeps his algorithm and adds a bound, as c5baef9 'Set tighter boundary on hypercube dimension' and 6a552f9 'Check overflow in intLoad()' do.

test_added: src/check/test_libmetis.c and test_libparmetis.c: bwgttab (9 six-decimal weights summing to 1) passed as tpwgts; checkPart. Pristine: archCmpltw error + double free.
notes: A zero target weight still fails (archCmpltw rejects null weights, METIS_ERROR returned); with patch 0001 it now fails cleanly.

our_title: V5 wrappers pick cut or volume from vsize presence, ignoring options[OBJTYPE]
severity_note: review says low; raised one step because callers asking for METIS_OBJTYPE_VOL get a partition optimised for the other objective and a wrong objval, silently; the partition itself stays valid
evidence: metis_graph_part.c:556 'return ((vsize == NULL)' :557 '? _SCOTCH_METIS_PartGraph (...' :560 ': _SCOTCH_METIS_PartGraph_Volume (...'; options[METIS_OPTION_OBJTYPE] is read nowhere in this file; metis_graph_part_dual.c:217-218 does read it
review_accuracy: accurate; its Fix line matches the patch. Assumption I make from the METIS 5.1 manual: METIS_PartGraphKway minimises edge cut (adjwgt) for OBJTYPE_CUT and total communication volume (vsize, NULL = unit sizes) for OBJTYPE_VOL, objval reporting the selected objective; real METIS rejects OBJTYPE_VOL for METIS_PartGraphRecursive (pmetis CheckParams) whereas the patch honours it there too, since Scotch's recursive strategy can run the same volume emulation (same leniency as the current code).

fix_options.label: a: keep the vsize-driven partitioning, report the requested metric only
fix_options.summary: After partitioning as before, recompute objval with _SCOTCH_METIS_OutputVol or _SCOTCH_METIS_OutputCut according to OBJTYPE.
fix_options.tradeoffs: objval becomes right, but the partition is still optimised for the wrong objective and the metric is computed twice; Kway wrapper only in the diff.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Half a fix; he already dispatches on OBJTYPE in PartMeshDual.

fix_options.label: b: dispatch on OBJTYPE in the common V5 routine (patch 0005)
fix_options.summary: objtval = _SCOTCH_METIS_optionGet (options, xadj, METIS_OPTION_OBJTYPE, METIS_OBJTYPE_CUT); CUT -> _SCOTCH_METIS_PartGraph (adjwgt, vsize ignored); VOL -> _SCOTCH_METIS_PartGraph_Volume (vsize, NULL = unit sizes, which it already supports); other values -> METIS_ERROR_INPUT.
fix_options.tested: cli19 (six cases), check_libmetis_v5 32/64-bit with new checkObjval() cases (VOL without vsize, CUT with vsize) which the pristine code fails
fix_options.tradeoffs: Behaviour change for callers that relied on 'vsize given => volume' without setting OBJTYPE (they must set it, as with METIS); doc sentence for OBJTYPE updated.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same dispatch as his PartMeshDual (metis_graph_part_dual.c:217-219) and the documented meaning of OBJTYPE in s_l.tex.

test_added: src/check/test_libmetis.c: checkObjval() computes cut and volume of the returned partition; cases OBJTYPE = VOL with vsize = NULL (Kway) and OBJTYPE = CUT with a vsize array (Recursive).
notes: PartMeshDual's output selection (vsize || OBJTYPE) is left to G26, whose CLI-05 patch rewrites those lines.
